epic.title: Animal-welfare operations vertical: the pet-rescue archetype ships a catalog, not an operating model
epic.description:
Driving a from-scratch install as a fictitious pet rescue exposed that the `nonprofit-community` / `pet-rescue` archetype ships a **storefront listing, not an operating model**. The public site is correct and the vocabulary is nonprofit-shaped, but nothing behind it runs a shelter.

## What already exists (verified against the schema, not assumed)

- `AdoptableAnimal` — a genuinely decent **catalog** row: name, species, breed, age, sex, size, description, `primaryPhotoAssetId`, `status` (available|pending|adopted|hold), and `attributes` JSON already carrying spayed/neutered and good-with-kids/dogs/cats.
- `StorefrontInquiry` (contact form), `StorefrontDonation`.
- **Canonical scheduling substrate**: `Resource`, `ResourceAvailability`, `ResourceCapacityPool`, `ResourceCapacityAllocation` — `Resource.capacityUnit` already defaults to `"units"`.
- **A proven vertical pattern**: `verticals-care.prisma` (CareAppointment + Participant + Resource + StatusEvent; CareIntakePacket/Response/AccessGrant/Exception/StatusEvent), `verticals-beauty-hospitality.prisma` (tables, `capacityUnit: "seats"`), `verticals-community.prisma` (governance), `verticals-storefront.prisma`.
- `StaffingShift`, `CalendarEvent`, `StorefrontBooking`, `BookingHold`.

## The gap

**There is no animal-welfare vertical.** Animals exist only as a listing inside `verticals-storefront.prisma`. Everything a shelter actually does each day is absent: where an animal is housed, who feeds it and when, what supplies that consumes, when the adopter is coming, which vet is treating it, what happened at intake, and what an open-house event is.

## The architectural finding underneath it

`ArchetypeVocabulary` is **eleven label strings** — itemsLabel, singleItemLabel, addButtonLabel, categoryLabel, priceLabel, portalLabel, stakeholderLabel, teamLabel, inboxLabel, agentName. It relabels one fixed process: priced items sold to customers. Note that every archetype must supply a `priceLabel`; `nonprofit-community` sets `itemsLabel: "Campaigns & Appeals"` and `priceLabel: "Goal"`.

**Processes are not abstracted across archetypes — they are re-implemented per vertical.** `CareAppointment` cannot schedule a vet visit for a dog because it requires `patientProfileId`. `hospitality-resources` cannot model a kennel because it hardcodes `kind: "table"` and `capacityUnit: "seats"` over an otherwise-generic `Resource`.

That is the decision this epic exists to force: **generalise the existing substrate to be subject-agnostic, or clone it per vertical.** The recommendation is to generalise, because the same question returns for every future archetype with a tended, housed, scheduled subject — equipment servicing, vehicle fleets, childcare, storage facilities. A kennel really is a restaurant table with a different `capacityUnit`, and that is an argument for finishing the canonical element rather than writing a third copy of it.

## Scope of the child items

Housing/occupancy; care scheduling; supplies; adoption appointments; vet coordination; intake pipeline including spay/neuter; events; funding beyond ad-hoc donations; and the vocabulary/process-abstraction decision that governs all of them.

Provenance: from-scratch reset/dogfood cycle 3, operator-directed deepening after the archetype was found to be catalog-only.

---

## Operating-model coverage: 0.28 (assessed 2026-08-22)

Worked example for the method in `docs/architecture/archetype-operating-model-audit.md`. Scoring: **2** = canonical or vertical-native model exists and the archetype uses it; **1** = exists but unreachable (vertical-bound) or partial; **0** = absent.

| Operational noun | Substrate finding | Class | Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| animal | `AdoptableAnimal` - species, breed, age, sex, size, photo, status | Canonical | 2 |
| donation | `StorefrontDonation`, wired to the storefront | Canonical | 2 |
| kennel | `Resource.capacityUnit` defaults to "units"; only the hospitality route consumes it | Vertical-bound | 1 |
| meet-and-greet | `CareAppointment` - good model, bound to `patientProfileId` | Vertical-bound | 1 |
| intake | `CareIntakePacket/Response/AccessGrant/Exception/StatusEvent`, patient-bound | Vertical-bound | 1 |
| adopter | `StorefrontInquiry` captures contact + message only; no profile or screening | Partial | 1 |
| event | `CalendarEvent` exists generically, not wired to the archetype | Partial | 1 |
| restricted fund | `FundBudgetLine` (verticals-community) is HOA member-equity shaped | Partial | 1 |
| foster home | absent | Absent | 0 |
| care round | absent | Absent | 0 |
| medication course | absent | Absent | 0 |
| supply stock | absent - a search for a Supply model returns nothing | Absent | 0 |
| application | absent | Absent | 0 |
| home check | absent | Absent | 0 |
| vet practice | absent | Absent | 0 |
| procedure | absent - searches for Procedure and MedicalRecord models return nothing | Absent | 0 |
| hold period | absent | Absent | 0 |
| grant | absent | Absent | 0 |

**18 nouns, 10 of a possible 36 = 0.28.**

**Decoys, recorded so nobody wires to them:** `InventoryEntity`, `InventoryRelationship`, `ContributorInventorySyncRun`, `ContributorInventorySnapshot` are the *codebase* inventory used for contributor source-graph sync, unrelated to physical stock.

An archetype below 0.6 should not be described as supported in external material. Re-score when this epic closes; the delta is the evidence the archetype improved.

items.title: Replace the Pet Rescue commercial value chain with intake, welfare, and placement streams
items.body:
## Problem

The Pet Rescue architecture currently projects a generic commercial chain—Attract & Discover, Capture Demand, Qualify & Schedule, Deliver the Value, Settle & Account, Retain & Grow, Trust & Compliance, Operate & Improve. That is not an animal-rescue operating model and makes "Capture Demand" look like the rescue's core work.

## Required operating model

Represent the animal journey as three linked primary value streams:

1. **Intake and safe placement:** stray/surrender report, retrieval or handoff, intake, identity, triage, quarantine, capacity decision, and kennel/foster placement.
2. **Health and welfare:** daily care, feeding and medication, veterinary assessment/treatment, rehabilitation, foster/kennel moves, welfare exceptions, and adoption-readiness decision.
3. **Adoption and placement:** animal promotion, application, screening, meet-and-greet, home/landlord checks where applicable, matching, reservation, custody transfer, post-adoption follow-up, and return/re-entry.

Fundraising, volunteer coordination, supplies, compliance, and reporting are supporting streams/capabilities. They should not overwrite the animal's progression.

## Scope

Update the canonical archetype definition and its EA/public projections for `nonprofit-community / pet-rescue`. Do not copy the generic nonprofit-category stream into every leaf, and do not hard-code a second Pet Rescue definition in the public site.

## Acceptance criteria

- Pet Rescue exposes the three primary streams above with clear inputs, outputs, stages, responsibilities, trust/approval gates, and handoffs.
- Capacity, quarantine, medical/welfare, foster/kennel occupancy, adoption readiness, custody transfer, and return are visible where they govern flow.
- The internal Architecture view and public Pet Rescue drill-down render from the same canonical definition and pass a drift test.
- The generic eight-stage commercial chain and "Capture Demand" are not presented as the Pet Rescue operating model.
- Category-level nonprofit language remains usable for charities, shelters, clubs, and cooperatives without pretending they share one leaf-level process.
- The view supports a readable list/table alternative to the graphical stream.
- Acceptance fixtures cover intake, welfare exception, adoption, failed placement/return, and capacity-full paths.

Blocked by: BI-2C80E6EA (subject-agnostic archetype process substrate decision).
Related delivery: BI-7111AF0C (intake), BI-5A25EC37 (daily care), BI-97290291 (veterinary coordination), BI-D2A51B36 (housing/occupancy), BI-A442F129 (adoption).

activities.summary: Pet Rescue three-stream model and projections pass

payload.body: 40 storefront tests, 5 DB projection tests, 3 EA table tests within the web suite, package typechecks, and public artifact drift check passed. Canonical page contains Intake and safe placement, Health and welfare, and Adoption and placement; Capture Demand is absent.

items.scopeRationale: The operating model and acceptance fixtures are specific to the pet-rescue leaf while reusing the shared archetype and EA substrate.

items.title: Archetype vocabulary is 11 labels over one fixed process — decide: generalise the substrate or clone it per vertical
items.body:
**This is the decision item. The other children of this epic depend on how it is answered.**

## The finding

`apps/web/lib/storefront/archetype-vocabulary.ts` defines `ArchetypeVocabulary` as **eleven label strings**:

```
itemsLabel, singleItemLabel, addButtonLabel, categoryLabel, priceLabel,
portalLabel, stakeholderLabel, teamLabel, inboxLabel, agentName
```

That is relabelling, not abstraction. It renames the surfaces of **one fixed process** — priced items sold to customers, with an inbox and a team. Every archetype must supply a `priceLabel`; `nonprofit-community` sets `itemsLabel: "Campaigns & Appeals"`, `priceLabel: "Goal"`.

An animal is not an item with a price. A kennel is not a menu category. No amount of label substitution expresses that.

## Where it bites, concretely

Two capabilities the platform **already has** cannot be reused by a rescue, for reasons that are incidental rather than fundamental:

1. **`CareAppointment`** (`verticals-care.prisma`) is a genuinely good appointment model — participants, resources, prep/recovery minutes, overbooking authorisation, recall, status events. It cannot schedule a vet visit for a dog because it requires `patientProfileId`. The subject is hardcoded to a human patient.

2. **`Resource`** (`resource-scheduling.prisma`) is already generic — `capacityUnit` defaults to `"units"`. But `apps/web/app/api/storefront/admin/hospitality-resources/route.ts` filters `kind: "table"`, writes `capacityUnit: "seats"`, and imports `restaurant-table-attributes`. A kennel is a `Resource` with `capacityUnit: "animals"` and nothing more exotic than that — the canonical element exists and only the vertical wiring is missing.

## The decision

**Generalise the substrate to be subject-agnostic, or clone it per vertical?**

Recommendation: **generalise.** The same question returns for every future archetype whose subject is housed, tended, and scheduled — equipment servicing, vehicle fleets, childcare, self-storage, plant nurseries. Cloning `CareAppointment` for animals means writing it a third time for the next one.

Concretely that means:
- A subject-polymorphic appointment (subjectType + subjectId, or a thin `AppointmentSubject` join) so the same engine serves patients, animals, vehicles.
- Finishing `Resource` as the canonical housing/capacity element and moving `kind`/`capacityUnit` into vertical config rather than route code.
- Extending `ArchetypeVocabulary` beyond labels into a **process profile**: does this archetype price its items; is its subject a person, an animal, or an asset; does it house subjects; does it schedule against them.

## Scope boundary

This item delivers the abstraction and migrates the two existing consumers (care, hospitality) without behaviour change. The rescue-specific work rides on it in the sibling items. Do not let it grow into building the rescue features themselves.

## Counter-argument worth recording

Generalising a clinical appointment model risks producing something that serves no vertical well. If the migration cannot keep `CareAppointment`'s clinical specifics (recall, overbooking authorisation) intact, cloning is the honest answer and this item should say so rather than force a bad abstraction.

Provenance: reset/dogfood cycle 3.


---

## DECISION MADE — start here

Run through the governed decision surface (`principle_decide`, 40 principles, governing profile `platform`, ledger **`DI-F289DBB51DCB`**):

| Option | Composite |
|---|---|
| **generalise-subject-agnostic** | **8.334** (winner, high confidence, autonomy-eligible) |
| hybrid-canonical-resource-first | 7.901 |
| clone-per-vertical | 5.136 |

**Generalise.** Clone is clearly last and should not be pursued.

**But the margin over the hybrid is 0.433**, only just above the 0.2 tie threshold. Treat the hybrid as a live fallback, not a rejected option: finish `Resource` as the canonical housing element first (it is already generic — `capacityUnit` defaults to `"units"`, and only `hospitality-resources` route code hardcodes `kind: "table"`), then attempt the appointment/intake generalisation.

If migrating `CareAppointment` cannot preserve its clinical specifics — recall, overbooking authorisation, prep/recovery footprints — **stop and take the hybrid**. Say so in the PR rather than forcing an abstraction that serves neither vertical. That failure mode is the entire reason the hybrid scored within half a point.

## Sequencing this implies

1. `Resource` as canonical housing/capacity; move `kind`/`capacityUnit` out of route code into vertical config; migrate `hospitality-resources` with no behaviour change.
2. Subject-polymorphic appointment + intake; migrate `verticals-care` with no behaviour change.
3. Only then the animal-welfare vertical rides on both.

Steps 1 and 2 are refactors with zero new user-facing behaviour. If either grows a feature, it has drifted.

items.title: Animals exist only as storefront listings: AdoptableAnimal requires storefrontId, so the 10 archetypes across 4 categories that manage living animals have no subject to hang care, health or custody on
items.body:
## What is wrong

`AdoptableAnimal` (packages/db/prisma/schema/verticals-storefront.prisma) is a **catalog
listing**, not an animal:

```prisma
model AdoptableAnimal {
  animalRef     String  @unique
  storefrontId  String              // REQUIRED
  name, species, breed, age, sex, size, description
  status        String  @default("available")   // available|pending|adopted|hold
  primaryPhotoAssetId, attributes Json, sortOrder, publishedAt, adoptedAt
  storefront StorefrontConfig @relation(..., onDelete: Cascade)
}
```

`storefrontId` is required and cascade-deletes. **An animal cannot exist unless it is a
published storefront listing.** So there is no way to represent:

- an animal in medical isolation or quarantine, not for public display
- an animal in a foster placement
- an animal that arrived today and has not been assessed
- an animal that was returned after adoption
- a cow, which is never a storefront listing at all

`age` is free text. `attributes` is untyped JSON. There is no weight over time, no health
record, no custodian, no location, no microchip, no intake date. Deleting a storefront
deletes the animals.

## Why this is the dependency root, not another gap

EP-5102F494 already has ten children — housing (BI-D2A51B36), care rounds (BI-5A25EC37),
intake (BI-7111AF0C), adoption (BI-A442F129), veterinary (BI-97290291), supplies
(BI-5E74E48C), funding (BI-E861E8B8), events (BI-7E3F4D4F), workspace (BI-7A38F667),
vocabulary (BI-2C80E6EA).

**Every one of them locates against an animal.** A kennel occupancy points at an animal. A
medication course points at an animal. A meet-and-greet reserves an animal. Built on today's
model they would all hang off a row that dies with the storefront and carries no clinical
identity.

The audit method orders children by dependency, not priority — "housing before care rounds,
because care rounds locate against housing". By the same rule, **animal identity comes before
housing**, and the epic is currently missing its own root node.

## Measured leverage: this is not a pet-rescue problem

Ten of 107 shipped archetypes, in **four unrelated categories**, turn on a living animal with
an identity, a health history, a location and a custodian:

| Category | Archetypes |
|---|---|
| `pet-services` | pet-grooming, mobile-pet-grooming, pet-boarding, dog-walking, mobile-vet |
| `nonprofit-community` | pet-rescue, animal-shelter |
| `healthcare-wellness` | veterinary-clinic |
| `agriculture-ranching` | cattle-ranch, mixed-farm-ranch |

Two of those already have open epics of their own: EP-5102F494 (pet rescue) and EP-55AF36AC
(Veterinary Clinic Operating System). A boarding kennel, a mobile vet, a shelter and a cattle
ranch all need the same subject; only the vocabulary and the custody relationship differ.

Solving it once inside `verticals-storefront` solves it for none of them, because that schema
is the sales surface.

## Evidence of absence

Searches over `packages/db/prisma/schema/*.prisma` returning zero:

- `Livestock`, `Herd`, `Paddock`, `Grazing` — 0 matches each
- no model relates an animal to a `Resource`, a `CareAppointment`, or a custodian
- `verticals-care` (19 models: PatientProfile, CareAppointment, CareIntakePacket, consent,
  coverage) models exactly this shape **for humans**, and nothing reaches it from an animal

## The decision this needs (resolve, do not defer)

`verticals-care` already models subject + intake + consent + appointment + resource properly.
The choice is:

1. **Generalise** — extract the care substrate to a subject-agnostic `CareSubject`, and let
   `PatientProfile` and a new `AnimalSubject` both specialise it. Highest value, touches a
   shipped clinical vertical.
2. **Clone** — new `verticals-animal-operations` schema mirroring the care shape. Safer, and
   duplicates 19 models' worth of design.
3. **Promote in place** — drop `storefrontId` to optional, add the operational fields to
   `AdoptableAnimal`, move it out of `verticals-storefront`. Cheapest, leaves the sales-shaped
   name and semantics in the substrate.

This decision gates the other nine children of EP-5102F494 and the veterinary epic.
It is closely related to BI-2C80E6EA (in-progress), which asks the generalise-vs-clone
question for the vocabulary layer — the same question, one layer down. They should be decided
together and by the same principle.

## How this was found

Archetype operating-model audit (docs/architecture/archetype-operating-model-audit.md),
step 3 (classify against substrate) and step 4 (hunt the canonical analogue), run during
dogfood reset cycle 4. `AdoptableAnimal` classifies as **Vertical-bound**, and the canonical
analogue is `verticals-care`.

payload.reason: The current AdoptableAnimal listing is not an authoritative animal aggregate. A partial model change before reinstall would split identity and lifecycle contracts.

deferral.reason: The current AdoptableAnimal listing is not an authoritative animal aggregate. A partial model change before reinstall would split identity and lifecycle contracts.
deferral.trigger: After reinstall, approve a canonical animal-domain design and fund an epic that owns migrations, compatibility projection, workflow adoption, and UX verification.

payload.rationale: Valid foundational animal-domain demand, but it requires a dedicated architecture slice across canonical animal identity, storefront projection, migrations, workflows, and UX. It is not safe to partially implement in the pre-reinstall drain PR.

items.title: DECISION: generalise verticals-care into a subject-agnostic care substrate so animals and patients share intake, consent, appointment and resource modelling
items.body:
## Decision

**Option 1 — generalise `verticals-care`.** Ratified by the founder on 2026-08-24 during
dogfood reset cycle 4.

Extract a subject-agnostic care substrate from the 19-model `verticals-care` schema.
`PatientProfile` and a new animal subject both specialise it, rather than either cloning the
design or promoting the storefront catalog row in place.

Rejected alternatives, recorded so this is not re-litigated:

- **Clone to `verticals-animal-operations`** — safer for the shipped clinical vertical, but
  duplicates 19 models' worth of design and guarantees the two drift apart.
- **Promote `AdoptableAnimal` in place** — cheapest, but leaves sales-shaped naming and
  storefront semantics embedded in the operating substrate, which is the original defect.

## Why this is the right call

`verticals-care` already models the exact shape needed: subject, intake packet, consent
directive, coverage evidence, appointment, participant, resource, status events, exceptions.
A shelter intake, a boarding admission and a veterinary visit are the same staged-admission and
scheduled-event-against-a-subject shapes the care vertical solved for humans.

Generalising is the only option that makes the 19 models serve all ten animal-bearing
archetypes instead of one.

## Scope

Parent finding: **BI-4F8A484C** — `AdoptableAnimal` requires `storefrontId` and cascade-deletes,
so an animal cannot exist unless it is a published storefront listing.

This decision gates the nine other children of **EP-5102F494** (housing, care rounds, intake,
adoption, veterinary coordination, supplies, funding, events, workspace) and
**EP-55AF36AC** (Veterinary Clinic Operating System).

## Coordinate with BI-2C80E6EA

`BI-2C80E6EA` is **in-progress** and asks the generalise-vs-clone question for the vocabulary
layer — the same question one layer up. It must be answered with the same principle:
**generalise the substrate, specialise the vocabulary.** Two threads answering this differently
would produce a generalised schema under a cloned vocabulary, or the reverse.

Whoever picks this up should read BI-2C80E6EA first and reconcile before writing schema.

## Constraint

Source changes belong in `D:\DPF-source-root` under its `AGENTS.md` contract, not in an
installed instance. Migration must preserve existing `AdoptableAnimal` rows — dropping
`storefrontId` to optional is a widening change and should be safe, but the audit method
requires re-scoring `pet-rescue` after the epic closes (it scored **0.28** on 2026-08-22) so the
delta is evidenced.

items.title: No daily care schedule: feeding, medication and welfare rounds are unmodelled
items.body:
Animals must be fed, watered, medicated, walked, cleaned up after, and observed — on a schedule, every day, whether or not anyone is thinking about them. None of that exists.

## What exists to build on

- `StaffingShift` — who is working when.
- `Resource` / `ResourceAvailability` — the housing units the work happens in (see the housing item in this epic).
- `CareAppointment` + `CareAppointmentStatusEvent` (`verticals-care.prisma`) — a strong model for scheduled, status-tracked events, but bound to `patientProfileId`.

## What is missing

A recurring care task tied to a subject, a time, and a person:

- **Task templates per animal or cohort** — feed twice daily, medicate at 08:00 and 20:00 for 10 days, walk, weigh weekly, clean the run.
- **Generation into a day's work list**, assigned to shifts, so the board a volunteer opens in the morning is the actual list of what must happen.
- **Completion with evidence and exceptions** — "ate nothing", "refused medication", "limping" are the observations that trigger a vet consult. A care log that only records completion is a compliance artifact, not an operational one.
- **Escalation**: a missed medication on a post-operative animal is a welfare incident, not a skipped chore. The `Cautious` autonomy stance a rescue is likely to pick should mean these escalate to a human rather than auto-close.

## Why this is the highest-welfare-risk item in the epic

Every other gap in this epic costs efficiency. This one costs animal welfare directly: an unfed animal or a missed post-op medication is the failure a shelter exists to prevent. It is also the work that volunteers — not staff — usually perform, which makes an unambiguous, assignable, checkable daily list the difference between a functioning rota and a WhatsApp group.

## Dependency

Depends on the housing item (tasks are located) and on the appointment-abstraction decision (a medication round is closer to a recurring appointment than to a to-do).

Provenance: reset/dogfood cycle 3.

payload.body: Start after the occupancy contract from BI-D2A51B36 and veterinary coordination contract from BI-97290291 are stable. Implement the Health and welfare stream without duplicating placement or appointment records.

payload.reason: Daily care scheduling depends on canonical animal identity, care-task ownership, staffing, recurrence, medication safety, and exception UX.

deferral.reason: Daily care scheduling depends on canonical animal identity, care-task ownership, staffing, recurrence, medication safety, and exception UX.
deferral.trigger: Resume after the canonical animal aggregate is approved and the funded animal-operations epic defines recurrence, assignment, medication controls, escalation, and operator UX.

payload.rationale: Valid rescue-domain roadmap demand, but it crosses durable data contracts, governed workflows, and operator/public UX. A backlog-drain PR cannot deliver the full acceptance boundary safely before reinstall.

items.title: No supplies inventory: food, litter, bedding and medication stock are unmodelled
items.body:
Animals consume food, litter, bedding, cleaning materials and medication daily. There is no model for any of it.

## Confirm before building: the existing Inventory models are unrelated

`grep '^model .*Inventory'` returns `InventoryEntity`, `InventoryRelationship`, `ContributorInventorySyncRun`, `ContributorInventorySnapshot`. These are the **codebase/contributor inventory** — the platform's own source-graph concept, nothing to do with physical stock. Do not attach physical supplies to them; the name collision is a trap.

`grep '^model .*Supply'` returns nothing.

## What to build

- **Consumables** with unit and current stock — dry food (kg), litter (bags), a specific medication (doses).
- **Consumption** driven by the care schedule rather than hand-counted: a feeding round for 40 animals depletes stock predictably, and the care tasks already know how many animals of what size were fed.
- **Reorder thresholds and alerts** — running out of a prescribed medication is a welfare incident, not a procurement inconvenience, and should escalate accordingly.
- **Donated goods in kind.** A rescue receives much of its supply as donations, which arrive unpredictably and are not purchases. Stock that only increments via purchase orders will be wrong on day one.
- **Cost per animal per week**, which feeds the sponsorship and funding picture.

## Scope note

This should be a modest, honest inventory — stock levels, consumption, reorder points. It is explicitly **not** a warehouse management system, and should not grow lot tracking, bin locations or barcode workflows in its first pass.

Provenance: reset/dogfood cycle 3.

payload.reason: Physical supply inventory is a separate bounded context from the existing contributor inventory and needs product, lot, location, consumption, reorder, and medication controls.

deferral.reason: Physical supply inventory is a separate bounded context from the existing contributor inventory and needs product, lot, location, consumption, reorder, and medication controls.
deferral.trigger: Resume after the post-reinstall animal-operations architecture approves a physical-inventory bounded context and funds schema, workflow, alerting, migration, and UX work.

payload.rationale: Valid rescue-domain roadmap demand, but it crosses durable data contracts, governed workflows, and operator/public UX. A backlog-drain PR cannot deliver the full acceptance boundary safely before reinstall.

items.title: Pet-rescue operating model re-scored 0.05 against a full operating day: 27 of 30 required entities absent, no intake, no housing, no holds, no medical, no outcomes, and the only animal surface is a 7-field storefront listing
items.body:
## Why this supersedes the 0.28 score

The 2026-08-22 assessment scored 18 nouns and returned **0.28**. That figure was optimistic
because the operating day it scored against was incomplete — it was written from what the
platform suggested rather than from the domain.

A full operating day (rounds, six intake pathways, stray hold clock, bite quarantine,
biosecurity ordering, foster, lost-pet matching, capacity pressure, outbreak contact tracing,
seizure/evidence holds, controlled-substance reconciliation, statutory reporting) yields **30
required entities**, not 18.

Re-scored: **3 of 60 = 0.05.**

- **1** — Animal, present only as a catalog row
- **1** — Photos, single `primaryPhotoAssetId` where a photo *set* over time is required
- **1** — Housing, vertical-bound but reachable in principle via canonical `Resource`
- **0** x 27 — everything else

The audit method requires re-scoring when the method or inputs change, or scores stop being
comparable. Full standing requirements:
`D:\Backups\dpf-reset-playbook\archetype-requirements-pet-rescue.md`.

## What the product actually ships

The entire animal surface is `/storefront/animals`:

> **Adoptable animals** — "These appear in the 'Animals available for adoption' section of your
> public storefront, each with their photos."
> **Name\*, Species, Breed, Age, Sex, Size, Description** -> *Add animal*

Seven fields, all marketing copy. Every `AdoptableAnimal` consumer is a storefront surface:
`storefront/animals/page.tsx`, `api/storefront/admin/animals`, `AnimalsSection.tsx`,
`AnimalsManager.tsx`. **There are no operational surfaces.**

The model name is the diagnosis. `Adoptable`Animal — an animal only exists once it is *already
adoptable*, which is the **end** of the shelter process. Everything that produces an adoptable
animal is missing: the stray report, the intake, the hold, the exam, the vaccines, the kennel,
the behavioural assessment. The platform models the last step and none of the preceding ones.

## Verified absent

Zero matches over `packages/db/prisma/schema/*.prisma`:

`StrayReport` / `FieldReport` / `IntakeRequest` · `Kennel` · `Euthan*` · `Vaccinat*` /
`Immuniz*` · `Microchip` · `Foster` · `WalkIn`

Decoys, recorded so nobody wires to them: `riskTier` / `hitlTier` match "tier" but are AI
risk fields, not cage tiers. `jurisdictions` on ai-coworker is a professional-practice scope
(`us|eu|uk`), not animal-welfare statute. `legalHold` in `verticals-care` is a records flag,
not a shelter hold.

## The legally load-bearing gaps

These are not features. Missing them means breaking the law or harming an animal.

| Gap | Consequence |
|---|---|
| **Stray hold clock** | Adopting or euthanising inside the statutory hold is unlawful and destroys an owner's property rights. Nothing models it, so nothing can block the action. |
| **Bite quarantine** | Health-department mandated, ~10 days, reportable. Absent. |
| **Rabies certificate** | Legally required controlled document, often county-reportable. Absent. |
| **Evidence hold (cruelty seizure)** | Animals held for court cannot be rehomed. Absent. |
| **Controlled-substance log** | Euthanasia solution must reconcile; failure is criminal. Absent. |
| **Outcome vocabulary** | Statistics and municipal contracts depend on a controlled set (adoption, RTO, transfer-out, euthanasia, died-in-care, lost-in-care, returned-to-field, disposal). Absent. |
| **Jurisdiction as a rule driver** | Hold length, quarantine, licensing and mandatory spay/neuter all vary by state and county. There is no jurisdiction input at all. |

**A hold must be able to block an action and explain itself.** That single capability is the
difference between a listing tool and a shelter system.

## Two design points that are easy to get wrong

**Housing position must include a tier.** Cat condos are routinely stacked two or three high, so
an animal's location is room + row + column + **tier**. A flat 2D grid cannot express where the
animal actually is.

**Housing placement must be a timeline, not a current-location field.** During a parvo outbreak
the shelter must trace every animal that shared a ward with the index case, including ones
already adopted out inside the incubation window. With only "where is it now", contact tracing
is impossible and the outbreak response fails.

## Canonical analogues already exist — this is smaller than it looks

Per the audit's step 4, most of this is reachable rather than new:

| Need | Existing model | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Housing unit | `Resource` | `kindSlug` is an open vocabulary ("chair, station, treatment_room, table, kitchen..."), `capacity` + `capacityUnit` already generic. A kennel is this with `capacityUnit: animals`. |
| Kennel layout | `OperationalSceneLayout` | Already generic, **not** restaurant-welded: `spaceKind` supports `cartesian-interior`, plus `layoutState` JSON and `underlayRef` for a floor-plan underlay. |
| Intake / consent / appointment / status events | `verticals-care` (19 models) | Exactly the right shape, built for humans. |
| Scheduling | `ResourceAvailability`, `ResourceCapacityAllocation` | Generic. |
| Photo sets | `MediaAsset` / `MediaAttachment` | Already many-to-one. |

Ratified direction is BI-51C95802 — **generalise `verticals-care`** into a subject-agnostic care
substrate. This finding strengthens that: the gap is reach, not absence of design.

Depends on BI-4F8A484C (animal identity independent of a storefront listing), which remains the
dependency root.

## UX

Credit where due: **`Simple` mode works.** It cuts navigation from ~25 destinations to 9 and
removes every builder and platform surface.

But the remaining 9 are generic business, not rescue operations: `Operations · Customer ·
People · Finance · Compliance · Portal · Knowledge · Coworker Decision Engine · All docs`.
"Customer" is wrong vocabulary — a shelter has adopters, surrenderers and finders. And **there
is no animal destination at all**; the only animal surface lives under storefront admin at
Portal -> Animals, filed under marketing.

So the finding is not that the UI is cluttered — that is already solved. It is that
**simplification reveals there is nothing operational underneath.** A kennel tech in Simple mode
still has no destination for the work they do all day.

Required role surfaces, with rounds as the highest-volume surface in the building: kennel tech
(one ward at a time in biosecurity order, one animal per card, large touch targets, single-tap
completion, one-handed on a tablet, tolerant of losing signal in a concrete block); intake
(chip-scan to hold-started in under 90 seconds with an animal in one arm); medical; adoption
counsellor; manager.

Full detail, definition of done and the 11-point acceptance list are in the requirements doc.

items.title: No intake pipeline: animals start 'available', and spay/neuter is a JSON boolean not a tracked procedure
items.body:
`AdoptableAnimal.status` starts at `"available"`. An animal that has just been surrendered is not available — it is unassessed, unvaccinated, possibly unneutered, and possibly contagious. The model has no way to say so.

## What is missing

The intake pipeline is the safety-critical spine of a shelter:

```
surrender / stray intake -> quarantine & observation -> health assessment
  -> vaccination, microchip, parasite treatment -> spay/neuter -> behaviour assessment
  -> ready for adoption
```

Today an animal is created directly as `available` with `attributes` JSON optionally noting spayed/neutered as a **boolean fact**, not a **tracked procedure** with a date, a provider, and an outcome.

## Why the boolean is not sufficient

`attributes: { spayed: true }` cannot answer: when, by which vet, at what cost, was there a complication, is the animal still in post-operative recovery, and is it therefore adoptable this week. Spay/neuter is simultaneously a legal precondition for adoption in many jurisdictions, a scheduled surgical appointment, a cost line, and a recovery period that blocks placement. It is a procedure record, not a checkbox.

## What exists to build on

`verticals-care.prisma` already has the right shape and it is close to reusable:

- `CareIntakePacket`, `CareIntakeResponse`, `CareIntakeAccessGrant`, `CareIntakeException`, `CareIntakeStatusEvent` — a full intake apparatus with exceptions and an auditable status trail.
- `CareAppointment` for the surgical/vet events themselves.

Both are bound to `patientProfileId`. See the abstraction decision item in this epic — this is the strongest argument in the epic for generalising rather than cloning, because the intake apparatus here is genuinely good and rewriting it for animals would be waste.

## Also in scope

- **Intake source** — owner surrender, stray, transfer from another shelter, born in care. Each carries different legal holds: a stray typically has a statutory hold period before it can be rehomed, which the platform must be able to represent or it will let a shelter break the law.
- **Capacity check at intake** — accepting an animal you cannot house is the decision this connects to the housing item.

Provenance: reset/dogfood cycle 3.

items.title: Workspace answers commercial questions on a shelter: no animals in care, capacity, care rounds or welfare exceptions
items.body:
The completed Workspace for a rescue answers commercial questions. A shelter's questions are different, and none of them are on the screen.

## What it shows today

**REVENUE IN $0**, **DELIVERED 0 jobs**, and a value chain of ATTRACT & DISCOVER -> CAPTURE DEMAND -> QUALIFY & SCHEDULE -> DELIVER THE VALUE -> SETTLE & ACCOUNT -> RETAIN & GROW -> TRUST & COMPLIANCE -> OPERATE & IMPROVE.

The header is right — *"LIVING BUSINESS — Pet Rescue: which mission commitment needs attention today?"* — and **LAPSING DONORS** is a genuinely archetype-specific panel. So the surface can already carry archetype-shaped content; it just mostly does not.

## What a shelter operator actually needs on opening the screen

- **Animals in care**, by status: intake/quarantine, in assessment, awaiting spay/neuter, ready for adoption, on hold, in foster.
- **Capacity** — units free by type and size. This is the number that decides whether the shelter can say yes to today's surrender call.
- **Care rounds outstanding today**, and any missed medication — the welfare-critical exception.
- **Today's appointments** — vet, meet-and-greets, home checks.
- **Animals with no adoption interest for N days** — the ones at risk of becoming long-stay.
- **Funds**: donations this month, restricted balances, cost per animal.

## The worker home already gets closer

The archetype's worker home is `Mission operations home` — *"which mission commitment needs attention today?"* — with Volunteer Program Board, Case Board, Communication Exceptions, Handoff Queue. Those boards are the right instinct, but nothing operational backs them: `verticals-community.prisma` holds only `GovernanceMeeting`, `RecordsRequest`, `FundBudgetLine`, `MemberEquityEntry` (HOA governance), so there is no volunteer or case substrate behind the labels.

## Dependency

This item is the **last** in the epic, not the first. Every tile above reads from a model that does not exist yet. Building the dashboard before the domain would produce a screen of zeros — which is precisely what it shows today.

Relationship to the copy item: the separate archetype-vocabulary finding (BI-D49C7245) covers renaming REVENUE/jobs. This item is not renaming — it is replacing the questions.

Provenance: reset/dogfood cycle 3.

items.title: No events: open houses, adoption drives and fundraisers have no model
items.body:
Open houses, adoption drives, vaccination clinics and fundraisers are how a rescue moves animals and raises money. There is no event model for them.

## What exists

`CalendarEvent` exists generically. `StorefrontBooking` and `BookingHold` exist for slot-based booking. Neither is wired to anything a rescue would run.

## What is missing

- A **public event** on the storefront — date, location, description, capacity — that supporters can see and register for. The generated rescue site has *Hero*, *Animals Available for Adoption*, *Support Us*, *About Us*, *Make a Donation*, *Get in Touch*, but no events section.
- **Registration / RSVP**, so the organisation knows attendance before committing volunteers and stock.
- **Animals attending** — an adoption drive takes a subset of animals off-site. That affects their location (housing item), their care rounds that day (care item), and their availability for meet-and-greets.
- **Volunteer roster for the event** — `StaffingShift` exists and is the likely substrate.
- **Outcome capture** — adoptions initiated, funds raised, new volunteers or fosters recruited. Without it there is no way to tell which events are worth repeating.

## Scope note

This is deliberately the lowest-priority item in the epic. It is genuinely valuable but it is the only one whose absence does not compromise animal welfare, legal compliance, or the organisation's ability to know where its animals are. Sequence it after housing, care, intake and adoption.

Provenance: reset/dogfood cycle 3.

items.title: No veterinary coordination: no partner practices, procedures, medical history or cost-per-animal
items.body:
A rescue's largest controllable cost and its main external dependency is veterinary care. Neither is modelled.

## What is missing

- **Partner practices** as external providers — which practice, what is the arrangement (charity rate, account, credit limit), who is the contact.
- **Appointments at an external provider** — spay/neuter surgery, vaccination, dental, emergency. These are appointments whose location is not the shelter and whose performer is not staff.
- **Medical history per animal** — procedures, medications with courses and end dates, allergies, chronic conditions, weight trend. An adopter is entitled to this at handover, and a shelter is exposed without it.
- **Cost attribution** — veterinary spend against a specific animal is what makes sponsorship ("Sponsor an Animal" already exists as a storefront item) honest, and what tells the organisation whether a given intake was affordable.

## What exists to build on

`CareAppointment` already carries `locationId`, participants, resources, prep/recovery minutes, and status events — a good fit for a surgical booking. Bound to `patientProfileId`. See the abstraction decision item.

No medical-record or procedure model exists anywhere in the schema (`grep '^model .*\(Procedure\|MedicalRecord\)'` returns nothing), so this is net-new regardless of the abstraction decision — which makes it worth designing subject-agnostically from the start rather than as animal-only.

## Connects to

Post-operative recovery blocks adoption (intake item) and generates medication rounds (care-schedule item). A vet appointment is therefore not an isolated calendar entry; it changes the animal's adoptability and its daily care for days afterward.

Provenance: reset/dogfood cycle 3.

items.title: Adoption is a contact form: no application, screening, meet-and-greet, reservation or return
items.body:
Adoption is the shelter's core transaction, and today it is a contact form.

## What exists

`StorefrontInquiry` — name, email, phone, message, `status`. The public site's *Adopt a Pet* renders as **Free / Enquire**, which is correct, and the enquiry lands here.

## What is missing

Everything between the enquiry and the animal leaving:

- **Application** — housing situation, other pets, children, landlord permission, experience with the breed. A rescue screens; a form that only captures a message cannot screen.
- **Meet-and-greet appointment** — a scheduled visit, against the animal, at a location, with a staff member or volunteer. This is an appointment in every sense the platform already models for patients and salon clients.
- **Home check** — a visit, often by a volunteer, with an outcome.
- **Decision and reservation** — `AdoptableAnimal.status` has `pending` and `hold`, but nothing links a hold to *who* it is held for or *until when*. Two adopters can currently be told the same dog is theirs.
- **Adoption record** — adopter identity, date, fee (a donation, not a price), and the post-adoption follow-up a rescue commits to.
- **Return** — the operator's own recorded stance is *"we take the animal back, always, no time limit, no fee."* The platform has no way to represent a returned animal re-entering the pipeline, which makes the organisation's defining promise unrecordable.

## Note on the fee

The adoption fee is a **donation toward that animal's care**, not a purchase price. It must not be modelled as `StorefrontItem.price`, or the accounting and the public copy both become wrong. `StorefrontDonation` already exists and is the right home.

## Dependency

Meet-and-greets and home checks are appointments against a non-human subject — see the abstraction decision item.

Provenance: reset/dogfood cycle 3.

items.title: Animals have no housing: model kennels/foster placements as canonical Resource occupancy
items.body:
An `AdoptableAnimal` has no location. A shelter's first operational question — *where is this animal, and is there room for another* — cannot be asked.

## The canonical element already exists

`resource-scheduling.prisma` defines `Resource`, `ResourceAvailability`, `ResourceCapacityPool`, `ResourceCapacityAllocation`, and `Resource.capacityUnit` already defaults to `"units"`.

`apps/web/app/api/storefront/admin/hospitality-resources/route.ts` builds restaurant floor management on exactly that: it filters `kind: "table"`, writes `capacityUnit: "seats"`, tracks `isBlocked` for out-of-service tables, and layers `restaurant-table-attributes`.

**A kennel is that same shape**: a named unit, in a zone, with a capacity, that can be occupied, blocked for cleaning or quarantine, and reported on. The operator's own observation was that kennel layout resembles restaurant floor layout — the schema agrees.

## What to build

- Housing units as `Resource` rows with `kind: "housing"` (or per-vertical `kennel`/`run`/`pen`/`foster-home`) and `capacityUnit: "animals"`, grouped into zones/wards.
- An occupancy link from `AdoptableAnimal` to its current unit, with history — animals move (intake pen → quarantine → adoption floor → foster).
- **Foster homes are housing too.** A rescue's capacity is largely off-site; a foster placement is an occupancy in a unit that happens to be someone's house. Modelling foster as a separate concept would fragment the capacity picture.
- Blocked/unavailable state with a reason (deep clean, quarantine, maintenance) — `isBlocked` already exists on the hospitality path.
- Capacity readout: units free by type and size, which is the number that decides whether the shelter can accept an intake today.

## Do not

Do not clone `hospitality-resources` into an `animal-resources` route. Lift the shared behaviour to a generic resource surface parameterised by `kind`/`capacityUnit` and have both restaurants and shelters consume it — see the vocabulary/abstraction decision item in this epic, which this depends on.

## Why it is first among the operational items

Care scheduling, intake, and capacity-to-accept all reference where the animal is. Housing is the spine the rest attach to.

Provenance: reset/dogfood cycle 3.

payload.body: Sequence this first because intake admission and daily-care scheduling need truthful kennel/foster occupancy. Coordinate with BI-7111AF0C and BI-5A25EC37; do not invent a second occupancy substrate.

items.title: Exercising the animals surface with real data: every animal auto-publishes to the public site on creation with no intake step, operational notes become public marketing copy, and Delete destroys the record with no confirmation
items.body:
## Method

Previous assessments of this archetype were made against an **empty** instance (0 animals,
0 accounts, 0 donations). This one exercised the only operational path that exists: three
animals entered through the admin UI, then followed to the public storefront, then a status
change, at desktop and tablet viewports.

Two of the findings below only appear once real records exist, and two earlier conclusions were
too harsh and are corrected.

## Corrections to earlier assessment — recorded first

**`hold` works, and I said it did not.** `AdoptableAnimal.status` offers
`available | pending | hold | adopted`, and setting `hold` propagates to the public storefront,
which renders **"On hold"** against the animal. The earlier finding that holds are absent was
about the *entity* (typed, clocked, concurrent, blocking) and remains true; but a single status
value exists and has real effect. Worth knowing before designing the hold model — the enum is
the seam to build on.

**The tablet layout is sound.** 768x1024: no horizontal overflow (`scrollWidth == clientWidth`
at 753px), and only five tap targets under 32px, one of which is the standard 1x1 skip link.
Given that rounds on a tablet are the highest-volume operator surface this archetype needs, the
responsive foundation being in place is a genuine positive.

## 1. Every animal auto-publishes on creation

Three animals entered; all three received `publishedAt` **within the same second** as creation,
`status = available`, and appeared on `/s/rescue` immediately:

```
Scout   | dog    | adult | status=available | published=2026-08-26 03:52:01
Marbles | cat    | young | status=available | published=2026-08-26 03:52:05
Pip     | rabbit | baby  | status=available | published=2026-08-26 03:52:09
```

There is no draft state, no intake step, and no review before an animal is publicly advertised
as adoptable. `available` is the default and publication is automatic.

**Scout was entered as "Found as a stray on Route 9."** A stray is under a statutory hold during
which it cannot lawfully be adopted out, because the owner may still reclaim it. The product
published it as adoptable in under a second, and the only way to prevent that is for a human to
remember to change a dropdown afterwards. The safe default is inverted: publication should be
the deliberate act, not the automatic one.

## 2. Operational data has nowhere to go but the public description

"Found as a stray on Route 9" is now **public marketing copy**, because `description` is the only
free-text field on the record.

In a shelter, found-location is operational data used for owner reclaim and jurisdiction, held
against the intake record. Here it must either be published or not captured at all. The same
applies to surrender reason, bite history, medical notes and behavioural flags — every one is
either omitted or shown to the public.

This is the storefront-shaped-model defect made concrete: there is no non-public place to write
anything about an animal.

## 3. Delete has no confirmation and no undo

`apps/web/components/storefront-admin/AnimalsManager.tsx:205`

```tsx
<button type="button" onClick={() => void deleteAnimal(animal.id)}
  style={{ marginLeft: "auto", fontSize: 12, padding: "4px 10px", ... }}>
  Delete
</button>
```

One tap, no `confirm`, no undo, no soft-delete. Measured at **59x28 px**, immediately beside the
status dropdown that a worker changes routinely, on a surface that works on a tablet.

The animal record is the subject everything else would hang off, and its photos cascade with it.
On current evidence this is the fastest path to irrecoverable data loss in the archetype, and it
sits one mis-tap away from a routine action.

**Suggested fix, in order:** a confirmation naming the animal; soft-delete with a restore window;
and moving the control out of the row's primary action area. A shelter also genuinely needs
*archive* rather than *delete* — an adopted or deceased animal must remain in the record for
statistics and for the statutory reporting the archetype requires.

## What this says about the archetype overall

The surface is coherent and works. It is a **catalog editor**, and it behaves correctly as one.
Every defect above is the same root cause already filed as `BI-4F8A484C`: the animal has no
identity independent of its public listing, so creating a record means publishing it, describing
it means publishing the description, and removing it means destroying it.

Related: `BI-4F8A484C` (animal identity, keystone), `BI-6AA4C3BD` (operating model 0.05),
`BI-9C5A3787` (vocabulary reach). Standing requirements:
`docs/architecture/archetypes/pet-rescue-operating-model.md`.

items.title: Nonprofit funding is donations only: no grants, restricted funds, municipal contracts or animal sponsorship links
items.body:
The rescue's funding model is represented by `StorefrontDonation` alone. That covers one-off and monthly giving, which the storefront already renders correctly (*One-off Donation*, *Monthly Giving*, *Sponsor an Animal*). It does not cover how most shelters are actually funded.

## Missing income shapes

- **Grants** — applied for, awarded, restricted to a purpose, reported on, with a deadline. Restricted funds are the important part: money awarded for veterinary care cannot lawfully be spent on a van, and an organisation that cannot represent the restriction will breach it eventually.
- **Municipal / animal-control contracts** — many shelters receive per-animal or per-year public funding to accept strays from a local authority. This is a contract with obligations (statutory hold periods, intake acceptance, reporting), not a donation.
- **Sponsorship attached to a specific animal** — `Sponsor an Animal` exists as a storefront item, but no link ties a recurring sponsorship to the animal it sponsors, so the platform cannot tell the sponsor how their animal is doing, or stop billing when it is adopted.
- **Fundraising events** and their proceeds (see the events item in this epic).
- **Adoption fees** — a donation toward that animal's care, not a sale (see the adoption item).

## Also missing: the nonprofit's obligations

- Charitable registration / tax-exempt status held on the organisation.
- Donation receipting to the standard donors need for tax purposes.
- Restricted-vs-unrestricted fund segregation, which is the core accounting distinction of a nonprofit and has no representation today.

`verticals-community.prisma` has `FundBudgetLine` and `MemberEquityEntry` for HOA governance — worth reviewing as prior art for restricted funds before designing new, though the HOA framing is member-equity-shaped rather than grant-shaped.

## Open question for the operator

The founder raised municipal funding as a possibility rather than a certainty. Before building, decide which funding mixes the archetype should support out of the box: pure donation, grant-funded, municipal-contract, or all three. The answer changes whether restricted-fund accounting is core or optional.

Provenance: reset/dogfood cycle 3.

I want a page that shows our foster families, which animals are staying with each one, how many more they could take, and when each animal is due back with us. What must stay the same: an animal in foster care must not show up on our public adoption list until the vet has cleared it.We need a foster homes page. It should show each foster family, which animals are staying with them, how many more they can take, and when each animal is due back. Fostered animals must stay off the public adoption list until the vet clears them.
